subject: Recap: Reliability & graceful-degradation needs — FinSecure discovery
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Ella Thompson <ella@finsecure.com>, Mark Johnson <mjohnson@finsecure.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Feb 2026 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Recap: Reliability & graceful-degradation needs — FinSecure discovery

Hi Ella / Mark,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the candid discussion about where reliability is tripping you up and the expectations your platform team has. Below is a short recap of what I heard plus proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Pain points (as discussed)
- Recent incidents take ~2–3 hours to recover; the Feb 1 incident had the biggest impact (users unable to complete auth flows).
- Primary concern: model-serving failures cause downstream cascade (timeouts against downstream services).
- No uniform fallback policy today: some endpoints retry, others fail-open with degraded UX.
- Capacity planning: unpredictable bursts from fraud detection jobs create saturation risk.

Current stack
- In-house transformer for low-latency routing (small ensemble) + occasional calls to external vendors for large-context tasks.
- On-prem data plane for sensitive workloads; cloud-hosted endpoints for lower-sensitivity routes.

Success criteria (what success looks like)
- 99.9% availability for inference endpoints for critical paths (auth, fraud scoring) with 95th pct latency < 300ms.
- Graceful degradation: deterministic fallback to smaller local model or cached response with clear user-facing messaging.
- Observable SLOs and an incident playbook with runbook steps for model fallback/rollback.

Immediate next steps (owner — ETA)
- Rishi: share Redwood one-pager on reliability and a short SLO draft (attached) — by EOD tomorrow (attached: redwood-reliability-onepager.pdf).
- Monica: provide SOC2 evidence snapshot and list of available security artifacts for their security review — target next Tue.
- Schedule: Demo of Dedicated capacity + canary/fallback flow — propose Wed 2/18 or Thu 2/19.
- Customer: Share the incident timeline + any runbooks you already have so we can map overlap.

Open questions we flagged
- Exact SLO windows you want us to propose (99.9% vs 99.95% for critical reads).
- Which workloads must stay on-prem vs which can be routed to hosted/dedicated.

I’ve attached a short SLO draft template and our reliability one-pager. If the high-level summary looks right, I’ll put together a short proposal and cost sketch for Dedicated capacity with staged fallbacks and a canary plan.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: redwood-reliability-onepager.pdf
From: Ella Thompson <ella@finsecure.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Johnson <mjohnson@finsecure.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Reliability & graceful-degradation needs — FinSecure discovery

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the concise recap — that matches our read. Couple of clarifications and additional context to make the proposal actionable:

More context
- Incident history: The biggest recent outage was Feb 1 (3 hours) when our async queue backed up and the external vendor timed out; impact was our auth flows and manual intervention was required. I’ll attach the incident timeline.
- Current SLOs: we have a 99.5% uptime target at the service level today, but for things like fraud scoring and auth we need closer to 99.9%.
- On-prem constraint: All PII or unencrypted traces must stay on-prem. Non-PII model calls can be routed to hosted/dedicated.

Questions for Redwood
- Can you show an example of a deterministic fallback flow (small local model + cache + circuit-breaker)?
- What kind of rollback/canary controls do you use for model updates (we need safe rollbacks with clear telemetry)?

We can share the incident timeline PDF attached. For next steps: Wed 2/18 works for a demo — Mark would like to see the Dedicated capacity plan + a canary example. Also, procurement will likely need an initial T&Cs/term sheet for budget planning.

Thanks,
Ella Thompson
Head of Platform Engineering | FinSecure
ella@finsecure.com | +1 (617) 555-0099

Attachments: incident_timeline_FinSecure_Q1.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Ella Thompson <ella@finsecure.com>, Mark Johnson <mjohnson@finsecure.com>, Procurement <procurement@finsecure.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 12:20:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Recap: Reliability & graceful-degradation needs — FinSecure discovery

Great — thanks Ella, that timeline is helpful. Quick reply with proposed commitments and schedule so your team can circulate.

Proposed short plan
1) Technical proposal & SLO draft (Rishi + Monica): we’ll produce a 1–2 page SLO proposal that maps to critical paths (auth, fraud) and proposed fallback behavior (local model + cache + circuit-breaker). ETA: 2026-02-12 EOD. (Attachment: SLO-draft-template.md)
2) Dedicated capacity demo + canary walkthrough (Stephanie): live demo showing capacity reservation, routing policies, and canary rollback options. Proposed: Wed 2026-02-18 14:00 ET. Stephanie will send calendar invite.
3) Security artifacts (Monica): SOC2 snapshot and list of evidence for procurement and security review — ETA: 2026-02-17.
4) Commercial: we’ll send a rough cost sketch and term sheet for initial sizing and commitment levels within two business days after the SLO draft.

Short answers to your questions
- Fallback flow: yes — we have a standard staged fallback pattern (primary model on Dedicated, synced lightweight model for local inference, then cached responses) with clear circuit-breaker thresholds you can tune. We’ll include a diagram in the SLO doc.
- Canary/rollback: we support traffic-sliced canaries with automated health checks and immediate rollback triggers tied to latency and error-rate SLOs.

Next actions (summary)
- Rishi: deliver SLO draft (02/12) + cost sketch after SLO.
- Stephanie: send demo invite for 02/18 and include run-of-show.
- Monica: prepare SOC2 snapshot and list of artifacts (02/17).
- Ella/Mark: confirm 02/18 14:00 ET or propose an alternate.

I’ll mark this as Deal RD-2026-0197 in our pipeline and follow up with a HubSpot link once I’ve created the record.

Best,
Rishi

Attachments: SLO-draft-template.md
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:55:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Recap: Reliability & graceful-degradation needs — FinSecure discovery

Forwarding the thread — FinSecure is looking for a Dedicated/canary plan and SLOs for auth + fraud scoring. Key asks: 99.9% availability on critical paths, deterministic fallback (local model + cache), and SOC2 artifacts for procurement.

Monica — can you pull SOC2_snapshot_Q1.pdf and any additional evidence we can share (encryption at rest details, key rotation notes)? Target 02/17.

Stephanie — can you prepare a 20–25 minute demo run-of-show that shows:
- Dedicated capacity allocation and autoscaling behavior
- Routing rules for critical vs non-critical traffic
- Canary deployment flow and automated rollback on SLO breach
- Cost sketch for 3 sizing tiers (pilot, production-small, production-large)

I’ll assemble the SLO draft and a short cost sketch and send to FinSecure by EOD 02/12. If you need additional context, see the attached incident timeline from the customer.

--
Rishi
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
